source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Gradual tapering is generally recommended to reduce withdrawal symptoms and rebound seizure risk in clients with seizure disorders, rather than stopping on their own schedule as the client is currently planning","B":"This is something that can generally be stopped with fairly little provider input or discussion beforehand, regardless of the reason for use, similar to what the client is currently assuming","C":"This is a medication that generally needs to be doubled in dose shortly before it can safely be discontinued, which is not an accurate description of how to stop this medication","D":"This is something that can generally be stopped abruptly with little concern for withdrawal symptoms or rebound seizure risk, similar to what the client is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Gabapentin is generally tapered gradually rather than stopped abruptly, to reduce withdrawal symptoms and, in clients with seizure disorders, rebound seizure risk.
source_row.stem: A client wants to stop taking gabapentin after several months of use, assuming it would be fine to just stop on their own schedule without checking in with the provider first. The nurse should instead explain that:
